note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §9, §13.7, Stage 66; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 35) on data/benches/seed.json: a supersaturated solution and a seed. The two beakers hold the same clear solution, 1.06 times what water holds at 20 C. A seed left still only grows; stirred, it breeds (secondary nucleation) and the solution's excess, about 1 g of the pentahydrate, comes out in minutes.
title: Experiment: supersaturation and a seed

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: Both beakers hold 50 g of water with more copper sulfate dissolved than it can hold at 20 C, yet no crystal has formed. A seed, one 10 mg crystal, will go into each; the right beaker will be stirred. How many grams of crystals do you think the stirred beaker will hold at the end? Type your guess, then click "predict".
steps.why: A solution that holds more than it can at its temperature is supersaturated. The extra stays dissolved until a crystal gives it somewhere to go: a crystal must start before it can grow, and a new one starts only rarely this close to saturation.

steps.title: A seed into the still beaker
steps.text: Pick up the left jar, then right-click the left beaker. In the menu that opens, click "tip in".
steps.why: The left jar holds a single blue crystal of copper sulfate pentahydrate, CuSO4.5H2O, 10 mg.

checks.text: the seed in the left beaker

steps.title: A seed into the other beaker
steps.text: Pick up the right jar, then right-click the right beaker, and tip it in.

checks.text: the seed in the right beaker

steps.title: Stir the right beaker
steps.text: Right-click the right beaker to choose it, then "stir" in the column on the right. Leave the left one still.

checks.text: time runs at least 60 times faster

steps.title: A shower of crystals
steps.text: Point at the right beaker and watch its crystals: their number, their mass.
steps.why: The stirrer knocks the seed about, and tiny fragments chip off it. Each is a crystal of its own and grows, and is chipped in turn: secondary nucleation. The more crystals there are, the faster the solution's excess goes onto them.

checks.text: 0.3 g of crystals in the right beaker

steps.title: The excess is out
steps.text: Wait until the right beaker's crystals stop growing.
steps.why: They stop when the solution is just saturated: about 1 g of the pentahydrate has come out, the copper sulfate water cannot hold at 20 C, with the five waters each unit takes from the solution.

checks.text: 1.03 g of crystals in the right beaker

steps.title: The still seed
steps.text: Now point at the left beaker.
steps.why: Its seed has only grown, by a few milligrams: one crystal, and the solution around it is still supersaturated. Left long enough it would grow into a large single crystal, which is how crystals are grown for show: a seed hung in a still, slightly supersaturated solution.

checks.text: the left beaker's seed still under 50 mg

fails.text: The left beaker was stirred: the two seeds cannot be compared now. Press reset to start again.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged

report.label: the crystals in the stirred beaker
report.why: Point at the stirred beaker and read its crystals. What came out is what water cannot hold at 20 C: 0.0656 mol of copper sulfate in 50 g of water is 1.06 times its solubility, and each unit that comes out takes five waters with it, so about 1.04 g comes out onto the 10 mg seed.
